Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

out adverb

out of the house, out of doors: go out, be out

also outdoors, out of doors, outside (direction), outside (position)

classical

Ter. Ad. 264: ipse exit forās
Plaut. Most. 1: Exī ē culīnā sīs forās
Traupman 355

forās

adverb, with verbs of motion

out (going out of doors)

Forās answers “where to?” and forīs “where?”: both are old cases of a noun for door, “out through the door” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • forīs — out, outside, out of doors (being out)

    adverb · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.19: cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret; Traupman 305; Traupman 355

    Forīs cēnāre, dine out. Also abroad, in public life, as against domī.

  • exeō, exīre, exiī, exitum — go out, come out

    verb, irregular (like eō), conjugation · classical · Plaut. Aul. 40: Exī, inquam. age exī.

    English “out” is often the Latin prefix ex-, ē-: exīre, go out; efferre, carry out; ējicere, throw out; ēmittere, let out. “He’s out”, not at home, is abest or forīs est (see away).

Examples

  • Exī, inquam. age exī.

    Out, I tell you. Come on, out.Plaut. Aul. 40

  • Manē, manē: ipse exit forās.

    Wait, wait: he’s coming out himself.Ter. Ad. 264

  • vēnit ad nōs Cicerō tuus ad cēnam, cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret

    your Cicero came to us for dinner, as Pomponia was dining outCic. Q. Fr. 3.1.19

  • cūrā ut valeās; id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre

    take care of your health; you will manage that most easily by dining out oftenCic. Fam. 9.24.3

  • ut forīs ita domī, ut in magnīs ita in parvīs, ut in aliēnīs ita in suīs agitāre jūstitiam

    to practise justice at home as abroad, in small things as in great, in one’s own affairs as in other people’sPlin. Ep. 8.2.2

See also out of, outside, away, away.
